lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 16, there are some additional factors I need to check. You can normally qualify for Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over if they're under 20 and staying in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, or an approved training program)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any approved education right now. He finished school but hasn't started college or anything like that yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's an important detail.

Since Alex is 16 and not currently in approved education or training, let me ask you this:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services? And if so, when did he leave education?**

(This matters because you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if he's registered with the careers service or anything like that. I don't really know if he's done that yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about not having that information.

Let me ask a couple more questions to get a clearer picture:

**Has Alex started any paid work? And if so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One more important question:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you currently live in the UK with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK with Alex. He lives here at home with me.

**Here's the situation:**

Since Alex is 16 and not currently in approved education or training, Child Benefit would normally stop. However, there's a potential exception: you can continue to receive Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks if Alex left education or training and has registered with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service, or

**What you need to do:**

To determine your eligibility, you'll need to find out:
1. When exactly Alex left education
2. Whether he has registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

If he has registered with one of these services and it's been less than 20 weeks since he left education, you may still be eligible for Child Benefit during that period.

I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific circumstances once you have this information. They can help you determine whether you qualify and what steps you need to take.
